title: AI Curriculum — One-Year Plan

depthMap.meaning: You have coded it once and can derive it closed-book
depthMap.areas: Reverse-mode AD; attention and the transformer block; the training loop

depthMap.meaning: Closed-book derivation; you read, not write, the code
depthMap.areas: Losses from maximum likelihood; generalization and regularization; the ELBO; MDPs and the policy gradient with baseline; DPO; the GRPO estimator; scaling laws; memory, FLOP, and dollar cost of training and serving

depthMap.meaning: One lecture and one paper; you can explain the mechanism and the trade-off, not reproduce it
depthMap.areas: CNNs and residual networks; diffusion (derivation followed, not reproduced); contrastive and multimodal models; tokenization and decoding strategies; attention alternatives and state-space models; parallelism schemes; FlashAttention; MoE; speculative decoding; PPO; alignment and safety landscape; the practitioner stack (LoRA and QLoRA, quantization formats, serving stacks, model merging, RAG pipeline components, LLM security)

depthMap.meaning: Named so the gap is known
depthMap.areas: Kernel programming; distributed-training internals; GANs and flows; classical ML beyond a fast pass; deep RL beyond policy gradients; mechanistic interpretability; formal verification; a research contribution

levelScale.3: transfers to an unfamiliar case and states the limits
levelScale.4: defends an original analysis under critique

competencyRule: A level is set only from a closed-book answer or an audited artifact, never from completing a resource; one competency per phase is retested 4–6 weeks later.

phases.name: CS primer
phases.exitCondition: Gate P: P3 and P5 exercises redone closed-book

phases.name: Phase 0: Foundation
phases.exitCondition: backpropagation built once by hand at toy scale; a 500-line PyTorch training script read and explained line by line; FLOP and memory arithmetic for a model done on paper; the six judgment questions in use.

checkpoints.text: micrograd with gradient check
Backprop-as-reverse-mode-AD derivation, one page
nanochat training script annotated

phases.name: Phase 1: Deep learning core
phases.exitCondition: a small GPT coded along once; the ELBO and the policy gradient derived closed-book; CNNs, diffusion, and RL understood at lecture level; a 2017–2022 architecture paper's ablation table predictable before reading it.

checkpoints.text: Toy GPT coded along, trained on a small corpus
Three closed-book derivations
ResNet notebook run with a one-page analysis
Fifteen paper notes

phases.name: Phase 2: Language models and systems
phases.exitCondition: you can account on paper for every FLOP, byte, and dollar in a training run described in a technical report, and explain every architecture choice in a current open-weight model.

checkpoints.text: nanochat model and tokenizer files annotated
Technical-report audit of DeepSeek-V4 with reported, derived, and unknown separated
Training-step cost derivation, closed-book
Benchmark critique

phases.name: Phase 3: Post-training, practitioner stack, reasoning, agents, evaluation
phases.exitCondition: DPO and the GRPO estimator derived closed-book; Raschka's GRPO notebook run and interpreted; one three-way agent comparison designed, run, written up, and threat-modelled; a system card followed back to its methods; and you can say what a team of yours would do to fine-tune, quantize, serve, and secure a model, and what each choice costs.

checkpoints.text: Two closed-book derivations: DPO, GRPO estimator
Practitioner artifacts: Unsloth SFT run and GGUF quantization run, each with a half-page of what changed and what it cost; LoRA and quantization memory arithmetic by hand
GRPO notebook run with a write-up of the reward curve and pass@k
Three-way agent comparison with Inspect eval, reliability memo, and OWASP threat model
RLVR-capability note and system-card note

phases.name: Capstone
phases.exitCondition: One bounded investigation inside what Phases 1–3 covered, run by an agent to your specification and audited by you, defended orally. The capstone demonstrates method, not a research result. An analytical capstone (a technical-report audit or a cost-and-decision analysis with a small simulation) is equally acceptable and fits a founder's use better than a training run.

checkpoints.text: Protocol and write-up
Audit log of the agent's runs
Oral defence completed; retest results recorded

weeks.lecture: Programming 1: variables, control flow, functions, strings, lists, dictionaries
weeks.reading: CS50P lectures 0–3; Think Python as reference
weeks.exercise: Five small programs without an agent: prime sieve, word count, a recursive function, a dictionary lookup, a file read

weeks.lecture: Programming 2 and numerical Python: classes, mutability, generators; arrays, shapes, broadcasting
weeks.reading: CS50P lectures 4–8 (selected); NumPy quickstart; From Python to NumPy ch. 1–2
weeks.exercise: Matrix class with operator overloading; matmul three ways, timed, ratio explained

weeks.lecture: Machine arithmetic and memory hierarchy: IEEE 754, bf16/fp16/fp8, cancellation; caches, bandwidth vs latency; what a GPU is
weeks.reading: CS:APP 2.1–2.4, 6.1–6.4; Goldberg 1991 §1–2; GPU MODE lecture 4
weeks.exercise: Why 0.1 + 0.2 ≠ 0.3; derive log-sum-exp; bf16 vs fp16; 4096² fp16 matmul time from FLOP/s and bandwidth

weeks.lecture: Algorithms and tooling: asymptotics, hash tables, graphs, topological sort; shell, git, environments, Jupyter, HTTP, JSON
weeks.reading: Roughgarden Part 1 ch. 1–2 and graph search; Missing Semester 1, 2, 6; MDN HTTP overview
weeks.exercise: Complexity of attention in sequence length; topologically sort a computation graph by hand; clone nanochat, run its tests, trace one stack trace

weeks.lecture: Information theory: entropy, cross-entropy, KL, mutual information, source coding
weeks.reading: MacKay ch. 1, 2, 4
weeks.exercise: Cross-entropy as code length; perplexity as exp(entropy rate); tokenizer as compressor. Gate P: P3 and P5 redone closed-book

weeks.lecture: Closed-book diagnostic (items in the Curriculum tab); Karpathy micrograd video, coded along, part 1
weeks.exercise: Ridge and cross-entropy gradients; error log; Value class with backward

weeks.lecture: Experimental judgment: leakage, baselines, judges, contamination

weeks.lecture: Prince ch. 3–5: shallow and deep networks, loss functions
weeks.exercise: Derive MSE and cross-entropy from maximum likelihood; universal-approximation sketch

weeks.reading: Adam 2014
weeks.exercise: Adam's invariance in its precise form; backprop through a two-layer network; variance-preserving init

weeks.reading: Nakkiran 2019; Power 2022; Dropout 2014
weeks.exercise: Paper notes with the six judgment questions; one page on SGD's implicit regularization

weeks.reading: ResNet 2015; Batch Normalization 2015

weeks.reading: Attention Is All You Need 2017; Layer Normalization 2016; Alammar, Illustrated Word2Vec, and colah, Understanding LSTMs (one hour: what attention replaced)

weeks.lecture: Karpathy GPT video, part 1, coded along

weeks.reading: Catch-up; optional nanochat speedrun
weeks.exercise: Closed-book: training-step memory and FLOPs under tensor and data parallelism; 7B on 64 GPUs budget. Competency rows 5 and 7 set
